name: @dezhouzhang/ihr360-ops-mcp

tools.name: ops_query_deployments
tools.description: Read one page of iHR360 OPS deployment records from /cmdb/deployments/. Requires a keyword. Returns app, environment, zone, cloud, host, hostname, and HTTP port. Read-only; it does not publish, restart, migrate, or run datafix.

keyword.description: Required OPS deployment search term, usually the app name. An empty search is rejected.

page.description: 1-based result page. Only this page is read.

tools.name: ops_resolve_image_version
tools.description: Resolve the latest eligible OPS publish-order image for one exact app. Selects the first success or standby row with a valid image tag. This is the same read JumpServer uses when a container is missing and image_version was not supplied.

app.description: Exact OPS application name whose latest success or standby image tag should be resolved.

maxPages.description: Maximum publish-order pages to scan before stopping.

tools.name: ops_query_applications
tools.description: Read one page of the OPS CMDB application catalog from /cmdb/applications/. kind must be datafix or migrate. Returns normalized app and HTTP port mappings.

kind.description: CMDB application catalog to read. Only datafix and migrate are allowed.

page.description: 1-based result page. Only this page is read.

tools.name: ops_runtime_diagnostics
tools.description: Report whether IHR360_OPS_USERNAME and IHR360_OPS_PASSWORD are visible to this MCP process. Never returns credential values, cookies, or CSRF tokens.

instructions:
This MCP reads the iHR360 OPS catalog at https://ops.ihr360.com. It is read-only.
Use ops_query_deployments to find where an app is deployed: environment, zone, cloud, host, hostname, and HTTP port. Always pass a keyword.
Use ops_resolve_image_version for the latest success or standby publish-order image of one exact app.
Use ops_query_applications for the datafix or migrate CMDB port catalog.
Do not use this MCP to publish, deploy, restart, migrate, or run datafix. Those executions stay on JumpServer.
Never invent OPS hosts or image tags when a query fails.
